properties.title: MM-DADM: Multimodal Drug-Aware Diffusion Model for Virtual Clinical Trials

membership.reason: MM-DADM models pre-dose to post-dose drug-conditioned 12-lead ECG transitions fusing ODE physiological priors (EPK) with causal drug-prototype disentanglement.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L2 drug-conditioned single-step physiological response world model (WT_PHYSIOLOGY, BP_FORECAST); author-claimed counterfactual comparison (L3) is not evaluated on matched patient alternatives.

properties.backbone: RBDCA diffusion with Dynamic Cross-Attention (McSharry ODE EPK) + contrastive CFE drug prototypes + CDC-Net

properties.flow: Pre-dose ECG x_pre + ODE EPK + drug prototype p_i + demographics -> CDC-Net diffusion -> post-dose counterfactual 12-lead ECG

properties.purpose: Simulating individualized drug-induced ECG changes (QTc, PR, Tpeak-Tend) for virtual cardiac drug trials.
properties.environment: 2 public PhysioNet clinical trial ECG datasets (9,443 ECGs, 8 drug regimens)

assertions.rationale: Causal Feature Encoder (CFE) extracting drug-specific latent prototypes from paired (x_pre, x_post) ECGs.
Dynamic Cross-Attention (DCA) adaptively fusing ODE physiological priors with noisy diffusion latents.

Pre-dose patient physiological state (12-lead ECG x_pre,j plus demographic covariates x_de,j and ODE physical prior x_ode) is explicitly carried into CDC-Net to predict the post-dose ECG state at nominal post-dose time points (0.5h-24h). Single-step pre-to-post-dose transition only (no multi-step recurrent rollout).
Explicit drug regimen conditioning via learned EMA drug prototypes p_i across 8 regimens.
Pre-dose to post-dose physiological state transition conditioned on drug assignment.
Diffusion model hybridized with McSharry ODE External Physical Knowledge (EPK).

Post-dose 12-lead ECG generation is conditioned on specified drug regimen, visit code, and nominal post-dose time point and evaluated across 9,443 ECGs and 8 regimens (QTc ACC 90.29%/REC 87.50%, PR ACC 91.14%/REC 91.18%, Tpeak-Tend ACC 92.16%/REC 93.45%; composite regimens 61.82%-84.31%; FRD 0.2431, RMSE 0.0127; Tables 2-4, pp. 6-8). Associational action-conditioning only; not causal identification.
McSharry et al. ECG ODE dynamical system fused via DCA.
Adaptive attention fusion of mechanistic ECG ODE trajectories and learned diffusion features.

One-step pre-dose (-0.5h) to post-dose (0.5h-24h) 12-lead ECG prediction is quantitatively evaluated against held-out real post-dose ECGs across 8 drug regimens (Tables 2-4, p. 6: QTc/PR/Tpeak-Tend ACC 90.29%-92.16%, FRD 0.2431, RMSE 0.0127; blinded 10-cardiologist visual Turing test 51.5%-55.0%, Table 5, p. 7). Single-step only; no multi-step rollout.
Virtual clinical trials for cardiac drug efficacy and cardiotoxicity screening.
Post-dose ECG QTc, PR, and Tpeak-Tend prediction accuracy (+6.13%) and recall (+5.89%) across 8 drug regimens.
Waveform morphological fidelity with/without EPK across 12 leads (Fig. 2).
Counterfactual demographic-drug recombination and drug-specific interval shifts (Verapamil PR, Quinidine Tpeak-Tend).
Expert assessments reported alongside quantitative metrics.

evidence_fragments.content:
To overcome these hurdles, we propose the Multimodal Drug-Aware Diffusion Model (MM-DADM), the first generative framework for generating individualized drug-induced ECGs. Specifically, our proposed MM-
DADM integrates a Dynamic Cross-Attention (DCA) module that adaptively fuses External Physical Knowledge (EPK) to preserve morphological realism while avoiding the suppression of complex pathological nuances. To resolve feature entanglement, a Causal Feature Encoder (CFE) actively filters out demographic noise to extract pure pharmacological representations. These representations subsequently guide a Causal-Disentangled ControlNet (CDC-Net), which leverages counterfactual data augmentation to explicitly learn intrinsic pharmacological mechanisms despite limited clinical data. Extensive experiments on 9,443 ECGs across 8 drug regimens demonstrate that MM-DADM outperforms 10 state-of-the-art ECG generation models, improving simulation accuracy by at least 6.13% and recall by 5.89%, while providing highly effective data augmentation for downstream classification tasks.

We fuse EPK into every denoising block via DCA (Figure 1a). Given that the DCA is a plug-and-play method, we specifically combine DCA with Residual Block [29] due to its effective framework for waveform generation, denoted by RBDCA.

Figure 3 demonstrates MM-
DADM’s precision in simulating drug-induced alterations. In Figure 3a, Verapamil extends atrioventricular conduction time: the subject’s PR interval increases from 167 ms to an actual post-dose of 293 ms. Our model closely mirrors this effect, predicting a 270 ms PR interval. Similarly, Figure 3b illustrates Quinidine’s prolongation of the Tpeak −T end interval. The subject’s true interval increases from a borderline 79 ms to an abnormal 142 ms, which MM-DADM successfully tracks by synthesizing a prolonged 153 ms interval.
During the validation phase, we generate the post-dose ECGs at specific time points by varying the drug information input to CDC-Net.

The results in Table 4 demonstrate that our method achieves the optimal FRD score of 0.2431 and an RMSE of 0.0127.

We combine the pre- and post-dose ECGs with the corresponding demographics and drug information into a real training sample. This means that for each subject, N samples can be generated, where N represents the number of time points at which post-dose ECGs are recorded.

capability_assessments.rationale: Downgraded from L3 to L2: MM-DADM implements a single-step pre-to-post-dose physiological state transition (019, 041) hybridizing DDPM diffusion with McSharry ODE External Physical Knowledge via Dynamic Cross-Attention (042), and evaluates drug-conditioned post-dose 12-lead ECG prediction across 9,443 ECGs and 8 regimens (043, 053; Tables 2-4). Although counterfactual demographic-drug recombination is used as a training-time augmentation loss (Lcau) and L3 counterfactual simulation is claimed (legacy_cells.AA), no reported evaluation compares >=2 alternative drug regimens on the same initial patient (action.comparison remains not_reported; matches legacy_cells.Z = 'L2 Action-conditioned prediction').

readiness_assessments.legacy_highest_label: R2 Public multi-regimen clinical trial ECG benchmark

limitations: Single-step pre-to-post dose synthesis rather than continuous multi-visit longitudinal rollouts.
Retrospective public trial datasets only; no prospective clinical trial validation.

Counterfactual demographic-drug recombination is used only as training-time augmentation (Lcau); no matched alternative-drug comparison on the same initial patient is reported (L2 demonstrated vs L3 claimed), and no causal identification assumptions are established.

legacy_cells.AI: 12-lead ECG waveforms; patient demographics; drug-regimen, visit-code and nominal-time-point information; ODE-derived ECG physical-prior waveform
legacy_cells.AJ: DDPM denoiser with bidirectional dilated-convolution residual blocks (RBDCA); CFE encoder; ControlNet trainable copy of RBDCA
legacy_cells.AM: Dynamic cross-attention adaptively fuses the ODE-derived physical prior into each denoising block based on discrepancy between prior and denoised features; demographics and drug features condition CDC-Net
legacy_cells.BD: Drug regimen/type; treatment sequence; visit code; nominal post-dose time point
legacy_cells.BN: Coupled cardiac ODE system generates an external physical ECG prior; ECG lead relationships are used to reconstruct four limb leads from leads I and aVF
legacy_cells.BV: DDPM noise-prediction loss; CFE contrastive loss; CDC-Net conditional denoising loss on real pairs plus weighted causal-guidance cosine-similarity loss on recombined counterfactual samples
